decisions.statement: A reading is kept in the file beside the readout the reading was taken for.
Where a readout's page sits is asked of the index rather than spelled.
A readout the index names no page for is refused rather than answered.
A reading taken for a page that is nowhere is refused rather than kept.
A reading never reaches the commit.
The file a reading is kept in never leaves the machine that took the reading.
The moment a reading was taken is kept beside its value.
How fast a reading falls with the clock is kept beside its value.
A reading no one says falls with the clock falls at nothing an hour.
A take naming a rate writes that rate.
A take naming no rate leaves the rate as it is.
A readout whose reading can fall names its rate on every take of that reading.
A reading replaces the reading before that reading.
A readout with nothing beside that readout has taken no reading.
A readout whose take answered nothing carries the moment it began answering nothing.
A readout whose take answered a number carries no such moment.
A readout answering nothing again leaves that moment where it already was.
That moment is taken away rather than blanked when a number is answered again.
Nothing is written for a readout whose answering is what it already was.
The key that moment is carried under is named here alone.
A reading in the file with one half alone is refused rather than read as no reading.
The reading a readout carries is read off the readout's own values.
The two halves a reading is carried under are named here alone.
The values a reading is written under are answered here rather than spelled by a writer.
Values with neither half have no reading.
Values with one half alone have no reading.
A reading is the number a readout is given to show.
Nothing here takes a reading.
Nothing here decides when a reading is due.

definition: the reading a readout last took, kept beside its page
